text: Why nq "took hours" before [computer]. Not reproduced. gap/c4_q3.g now prints the wall time per stage. On the Modal container (GAP 4.14 from Debian trixie, nq from gap-nq), with the weight-5 commutators not passed to nq (Q3_NQTOP := false; they are redundant for class := 4, and they stay in the output relators): nq takes 4 s for the infinite Rd4, Rd6 and 132 s (Rf15, Rd46f15), 267 s (Rf16) for the finite ones — the large exponents $2^{15},2^{16}$ cost nq a factor 30–60, but minutes, not hours. The rest of GAP is the same for all: lower central series about 1 s, abelian invariants and the snf basis of $\gamma_4$ 30–43 s, exponents of the 540 commutators 8 s, and then about 570 s (90 % of GAP's CPU time) for the one remaining step, the check that the extra test word $w$ lies in $\gamma_4(M)$ and is nontrivial (MappedWord of a long word into the pcp group and membership in $\gamma_4$) — that, not nq, is what makes a base take 10 min (presumably also for the R2 bases above, whose logs have no stage times). Whether the hours in Docker came from the 3240 redundant relators given to nq for a finite group, or from the memory of the Docker VM, was not tested.

text: So for the first pass of §6.6 the test "for all $K$" is now done at the decisive $n$ for every base: the plateau P6, the 12 R2 bases (Rk14, …, Rk56, Rd46, Rd46f15) and the 4 R bases (Rd4, Rd6, Rf15, Rf16) — $D_7(M/K)=1$; the 40 T and 16 S bases — $D_5(M/K)=1$; the 7 L bases — $D_6(M/K)=1$. Summary of the first pass of class 4 [computer + on paper]: for each of the 80 bases $\Gamma$ of §6.6 and every $K\subseteq\gamma_4(M)$, $M=\Gamma/\gamma_5(\Gamma)\Gamma''$, the group $M/K$ has $D_7=1$ (P6, R, R2: 17 bases), $D_6=1$ (L: 7) or $D_5=1$ (T, S: 56). In particular no metabelian group of class 4 obtained from these presentations by a central modification of $\gamma_4$ has $D_7\ne1$; finding one needs a base $\Gamma$ outside this family.

text: The ring (§6.7, last paragraph). $L'_N$: the free metabelian Lie ring on $x_1..x_4$, Hall order $x_3<x_1<x_2<x_4$, $t=[x_4,x_3,\dots,x_3]$ ($N$ letters $x_3$), $c_i=[t,x_i]$, $u_i=[c_i,x_i]$, the relators $r_1=4x_1+2c_3+c_2$, $r_2=16x_2+4c_3-c_1$, $r_3=64x_3-4c_2-2c_1$, (ii) $\gamma_{N+4}=0$, (iii) every Hall basis element of weight $N+3$ other than $u_1,u_2,u_3$ is $0$, (iv) $u_1=16u_3$, $u_2=4u_3$, $64u_3=0$; $a=32[x_1,x_2]+64[x_1,x_3]+128[x_2,x_3]$. text: The plateau is forced by the grading [on paper]. In the component of $a$ (degree 2) a word with $k$ letters $x_4$ has $2+Nk$ other letters, so its length is $2+(N+1)k\in\{2,\,N+3,\,2N+4,\dots\}$; the same holds for $L_N$ of [IMP26] with the grading $\deg x_5=(0,1)$, $\deg x_4=(0,-N)$, $\deg x_{1,2,3}=(1,0)$. Since $\varpi^n$ is spanned by the words of length $\ge n$, $\varpi^{N+4}\cap U(L)_2=\varpi^{2N+4}\cap U(L)_2$, hence $D_{N+4}\cap L_2=D_{2N+4}\cap L_2$: once $D_{N+4}\subseteq L_2$, the length $N+1$ of the plateau is the gap between the admissible lengths $N+3$ and $2N+4$. (Computed: for $N=2$ the component of $a$ in $A_6,A_7,A_8$ is the same 414 columns and 1 791 rows.) A group ring has no such grading: $\mu(x^E)-1=\sum_k\binom Eka^k$ mixes all lengths.

text: The group analogue [computer]. The literal translation L2g (gap/plateau5_cands.g, family I5cand, $d=4$): $t=[x_4,x_3,x_3]$, $d_l=[t,x_l]$, $$x_1^4d_2d_3^2,\quad x_2^{16}d_1^{-1}d_3^4,\quad x_3^{64}d_1^{-2}d_2^{-4},\quad [d_1,x_1][d_3,x_3]^{-16},\quad [d_2,x_2][d_3,x_3]^{-4},\quad[d_3,x_3]^{64},\quad[d_l,x_m]\ (l\ne m),\ [d_4,x_4],$$ $w=[x_1,x_2^{32}][x_1,x_3^{64}][x_2,x_3^{128}]$ (the image of $a$). Then $G_{\rm ab}=\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/4\oplus\mathbb Z/16\oplus\mathbb Z/64$ as for $L'_2$, $\gamma_5(G)\cong\mathbb Z/64=\langle u_3\rangle$, $u_3=[d_3,x_3]$, $w=u_3^{32}$; GAP 13 min. Tests of $u_3^{2^j}$ (CPU, howell_gpu.py, certified): $D_5\cap\gamma_5=\gamma_5$, $D_6\cap\gamma_5=\langle w\rangle$, $D_7\cap\gamma_5=1$. The group analogue stops at $D_6$, two levels below the ring. With $L_{ij}$ doubled or quadrupled, $w=1$ already in $M$.
